Fix uses type_changed's Option<(old,new)> — when the type LEAVES Reference, emit ALTER TABLE ... DROP CONSTRAINT before the retype (drops by the pre-rename field name if the same bump renames it); when it ENTERS Reference, emit fk_op ADD CONSTRAINT after the retype; a Reference re-pointed at a new target does both. Owner decision (dkk, 2026-08-15) implemented in clients/loop-console/src/reader/run-vocabulary.ts: the reader keeps the WIRE run vocabulary, and screens translate through a named mapping.

THE SURVIVOR IS A FINDING. digest-uses-the-other-canonicalizer swaps ServingManifest::digest onto the workspace's private ryu-js canonicalizer and ALL tests stay green — the two RFC 8785 implementations agree byte-for-byte on manifest-shaped documents (every field a string, an integer, or a map of them; the shape never reaches the number or escape paths where they could diverge). Commit 5064a4da. [47b404cf] wamn_db_owner NOLOGIN now owns every project-env database; wamn_app holds CONNECT only. Zero grants, zero memberships, no password, no generation pair -- it holds title and nothing connects as it, so nothing rotates. *** OPERATOR HAZARD MEASURED AND NOT IN ANY BRIEF: ALTER DATABASE ... OWNER TO DESTROYS wamn_app's CONNECT GRANT. With wamn_app as owner, datacl is {wamn_app=CTc/wamn_app} -- the explicit GRANT CONNECT MERGES INTO THE OWNER'S ACLITEM -- so changing the owner rewrites it and wamn_app loses CONNECT outright. Correct end state {wamn_db_owner=CTc/wamn_db_owner,wamn_app=c/wamn_db_owner}. An operator who applies the new CR and stops leaves the runtime UNABLE TO REACH ITS OWN DATABASE. The owner change is emitted FIRST and the privilege SQL is MANDATORY on existing environments; documented at both emission sites. *** Convergence is the reconciler's job: re-setting an existing owner is a no-op (verified by applying the batch twice) and CNPG maps spec.owner to both CREATE DATABASE OWNER and ALTER DATABASE OWNER TO, so existing CRs converge. No one-shot script. MUTATION-VERIFIED: owner set back to APP_ROLE turns the ownership probe red; restored. pg_shdepend zero-owned-objects carries a non-vacuity counter-assert of 2. PREMISE CORRECTION: ensure_effect_writer_acl_role_sql has NO advisory lock -- the advisory-locked create-or-harden house shape is ensure_control_author_acl_role_sql, which was followed (it also re-hardens on attribute drift, and avoids duplicating a gate-mutant NEEDLE literal). Closes finding R45. DEFERRED, filed separately: provision-project (legacy 2.3) creates postgres-owned databases -- create_database_sql has no OWNER clause -- the other failure mode the ruling names.

[47b404cf] The PUBLIC CONNECT floor looped WHERE NOT datistemplate, and template1 is datallowconn=true with PostgreSQL's default PUBLIC CONNECT -- so wamn_app could log into template1 on every cluster and from there ALTER or DROP every database it owned while holding CONNECT on none. That is what made the database-ownership authority trivially reachable. Filter is now datallowconn: includes template1, still excludes template0. *** NOT every datistemplate site moved, deliberately: non_template_databases_sql KEEPS the template filter because its caller OPENS A CONNECTION to every name it returns, and an open template1 session breaks concurrent CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE template1. The asymmetry is documented in place so a future consistency edit does not cause an outage. *** MUTATION-VERIFIED: filter set back to NOT datistemplate turns the template1 probe red; restored. Verified no workload connects to template1 or postgres as a non-superuser, and that CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE template1 needs no CONNECT (proved with a non-superuser CREATEDB role holding none). The m1 gate is unaffected -- the floor never runs there; its only callers are provision_project_env and the effect-writer live test, which passes green with the widened floor.

[47b404cf] grant_replication_access_sql granted the CDC role SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA -- every tenant data table -- justified as needing reads for an initial snapshot, while its own next clause said decoding reads WAL not tables. The shipped reader performs no snapshot: its only project-env table query is the entity map (cdc-reader/src/lib.rs:317), and StreamingMode::Off is the pgoutput in-progress-transaction option, not a snapshot. This was a CONFIDENTIALITY over-grant, not tidiness: the replication path is gated by the REPLICATION attribute, the walsender protocol and slot ownership, and this grant gave the SAME CREDENTIAL a plain SQL read of all tenant data with none of those gates. Narrowed to the entity map WITH A RETROACTIVE REVOKE -- without it the fix reaches only new environments, the single most likely way it would have landed incompletely. MUTATION-VERIFIED: dropping the retroactive REVOKE turns the new test red while the OLD one still passes (exactly the gap it was written to catch); swapping REVOKE/GRANT order turns both red; restored. Decoding of a table the role cannot SELECT still yields frames. NOINHERIT added for exactness (the only role in the repo defaulting to INHERIT); inert today since the role holds no memberships, and existing roles keep INHERIT because the IF NOT EXISTS guard is retained. The REPLICATION attribute is untouched -- it is an attribute, not a grant, and removing it breaks logical decoding outright. Blast radius stays wamn-0h0g.12.68, still unruled.

THE FAILURE MODE MATTERED MORE THAN THE FALSE POSITIVE: the panic tells the next author to 'add to the allowlist', and the allowlist is the one edit that genuinely weakens this guard. [e96bb401] The reconciler returned Ok(Vec::new()) when catalog.event_registrations was merely ABSENT; the pure planner cannot distinguish that from "no entity needs FULL", so it planned a reset to DEFAULT for every table at FULL -- a NON-RETROACTIVE flip presenting as a clean idempotent run. Now refuses by name: replica-identity-registrations-absent / -unreadable, in the crate's existing PublicationError shape. *** THE SILENT THIRD STATE WAS THE DANGEROUS ONE and it could NOT be deferred: the table is FORCE RLS, so a non-bypassing session reads zero rows with NO error, and the module's own doc advertised "a superuser (OR THE SCHEMA OWNER)" as supported -- FORCE strips the owner's exemption and PostgreSQL checks BYPASSRLS on the current role only, so the documented-supported credential WAS the silent full reset. The cross-tenant read now runs under row_security = off (the pg_dump idiom) so PostgreSQL raises 42501 instead of filtering; inert for asuperuser. *** PREMISE CORRECTION: never a CronJob-only exposure -- publish_catalog's call site is dead under .8.18's unconditional bail, but migrate_catalog.rs:178 is live and unclosed, and ri_orch_live is consequently red on baseline and no longer covers reconcile_after_apply. New gate replica_identity_unreadable_live proves absent + RLS-hidden refuse on dry-run AND apply with 'f' intact, demonstrates the silence directly, and proves a genuinely-empty provisioned env still reconciles including the legitimate reset direction, idempotently, inside a caller's open transaction with no GUC leak. Precision pair re-derived AT INTEGRATION: restoring the early return turns the refusal test RED (printing ReplicaIdentityFlip orders/sales_orders Full->Default) and leaves the positive test GREEN; restored byte-identical by sha256 and re-verified. [3ae75699] Version-keyed wiring resolution cache landed in the new crates/execution/router/src/resolution.rs, modelled on ResolutionPlanCache's shape verbatim (Mutex<CacheState>, HashMap + VecDeque recency, touch() on hit, evict from the front) with the one structural difference the bead demanded: it INVALIDATES rather than never. *** DESIGN CALL WORTH RATIFYING — THE CACHE IS TWO LEVELS, AND IT HAS TO BE. The bead asked for a key of (env, wiring id, active version) AND invalidation on pointer flip; those only cohere if the cache also holds the pointer, because otherwise you must already know the active version to look anything up, i.e. you have already read Postgres. So: entries: HashMap<EntryKey, Arc<Wiring>> on the full triple (a version is IMMUTABLE — catalog.wirings.version monotonic, content pinned by confirmed_definition_hash — so a resident entry can never be the wrong answer to its own key), plus active: HashMap<Pointer, u32> mirroring catalog.wiring_activation as the ONLY mutable half and the only half invalidate touches. It pays off on ROLLBACK: a flip back to a still-resident version is an in-memory hit. One addition the model does not need — an evicted entry drops the pointer that named it, so a pointer can never read as a hit and find nothing (pinned by an_evicted_entry_leaves_behind_no_pointer). *** METRIC: one counter wamn.run.wiring.cache.lookups split by a two-valued result=hit|miss attribute, so the hit rate — the number that says whether the hot path is actually staying out of Postgres — is a single query; no wiring/tenant attribute (unbounded). Registered via the same global-meter pattern as memory_metrics.rs:56. DEPENDENCY ACCEPTED, FLAGGED: opentelemetry with the metrics feature added to a crate that previously had exactly one dependency. Integrator verified the Cargo.lock delta is a SINGLE LINE (+ opentelemetry under wamn-router), no version churn, no new crate; the bead explicitly scopes a cache-hit metric, so this is proportionate. Reversible by moving the counter to the host. LANDED as commit 200517a4 on deploy-simplification. Premise CONFIRMED, not refuted: reproduced as ERROR LOCK TABLE can only be used in transaction blocks at catalog-schema.sql:1218 under psql autocommit. FIX: wrapped the WHOLE FILE in BEGIN/COMMIT, not just the LOCK. Wrapping only the LOCK region would have BROKEN PRODUCTION - under batch_execute a mid-file BEGIN promotes the already-open implicit transaction to explicit, so the COMMIT would commit everything before it and split the file's atomicity into segments. Whole-file wrapping is today's production semantics made explicit. PROVEN BOTH WAYS against postgres:18.6: psql -f autocommit exit 0 (was 3); the batch_execute wire shape exit 0; and atomicity verified by replacing the closing COMMIT with SELECT 1/0, after which the catalog schema was absent, so it is still one transaction. THE SWEEP, which this bead required to close: FIVE appliers feed deploy/sql/*.sql to a non-transactional client, not one - read_authority.rs (the defect site), ops_storage.rs, control_storage.rs, project-state/tests/schema.rs and authority.rs; the last four were clean. Exactly ONE illegal statement exists: the bare LOCK. The two LOCKs in control-portable-store.sql sit inside DO blocks, which always run in a transaction, and were measured legal. THE INVERSE CLASS WAS ALSO SWEPT: only postgres-init.sql is illegal INSIDE a transaction (CREATE DATABASE plus the psql meta-command backslash-connect); it is psql-only by construction and must NOT be wrapped. Reconciler-generated SQL audited too - every LOCK TABLE in run_plane.rs reaches PostgreSQL via batch_execute, so a lone-LOCK action would fail, but every emitter always pairs the LOCK with at least one DO, ALTER or DROP, so no lone-LOCK action exists. Consequential edits in run_plane.rs: table_section now stops at COMMIT so a repair action does not carry transaction control into the caller's batch. required-gate it replaces - still a gate, no longer required. Reusing partial-proof was
rejected because its one existing user, D15-WRITE-AHEAD-ADMISSION, means the gate really does

empty decision_ids for them and forbids can_fail - so parking that way would silently delete
the D3 and D19 linkage. Measurement and Drill fit structurally but neither word means parked,

FOUR PREMISE CORRECTIONS, ALL MEASURED BEFORE IMPLEMENTING.
1. The schema is wamn_authority, not wamn. The two qualified names now live in wamn-pg-core, the dependency-free leaf both the provisioner that CREATES the functions and the compiler that EMITS CALLS to them already use, so there is one definition rather than one per crate.
2. The predicate needed a session side that did not exist. Filed and landed as wamn-0h0g.22.6.5 first.
3. The index name enters the SHARED pg_class namespace, so the suffix is _tkey - exactly the width of _pkey, which is what ENTITY_NAME_BUDGET already reserves. A wider suffix would have shrunk that budget and invalidated catalogs that are valid today, and PostgreSQL truncates an over-long identifier with a NOTICE rather than refusing.
4. A SYNTHESIZED RELATION NAME IS NOT JUST AN EMIT. The tenant-key index also had to enter migrate_plan's all_relnames collision scan, the index_asides set for a dropped table whose name is reclaimed, a rename op that follows the table rename the way <table>_pkey does, and wamn-schema-model's derive_identifiers. Omitting any of those is the deletion-collateral class inverted.

THE DRIFT GUARD WAS BLIND AND IS NOT ANY MORE. synthesized_identifiers_cover_every_emitted_relation_and_constraint matched CREATE INDEX at the START of an operation, and the tenant-key index is emitted INSIDE the multi-statement RLS floor whose first line is an ALTER TABLE - so it would have reported full coverage it did not have. It now scans per LINE and names the tenant-key index explicitly.

WHY IT EXISTS. Measuring split 3 hit a constraint no bead named: tenant_key bakes the database name in as a LITERAL because current_database() is STABLE and would make the function non-indexable, but catalog-schema.sql and app-schema.sql are STATIC files applied to project-environment databases whose names are unknown when the file is authored. Neither can carry a literal, and split 3 could not re-key a single static-file policy without this.

WHAT LANDED. ONE TEMPLATE, TWO RENDERINGS. derivations_template takes the database literal and its octet length as pre-rendered fragments; authority_derivations_sql substitutes a real name, authority_derivations_bootstrap_sql substitutes placeholders and wraps the whole thing in a DO block that fills them from current_database() at APPLY time and EXECUTEs the result. The installed function is IMMUTABLE either way, because the name is baked in as a literal rather than read at call time. quote_literal runs on the SERVER, so a database name containing a quote cannot break out of the body.

SHARING A TEMPLATE IS NOT THE PROOF. the_bootstrap_and_literal_renderings_install_the_same_object applies BOTH renderings into one database and asserts md5(pg_get_functiondef) is identical for both functions. That is the digest probe wamn-0h0g.22.6.1 created doing exactly the job it was created for: one pin, two appliers, zero drift tolerance. It also reads IMMUTABLE from pg_proc, builds the expression index, and checks the bootstrapped value against Rust across all seven boundary tenants.

*** THE GATE USES A MULTI-BYTE DATABASE NAME ON PURPOSE. *** The bootstrap counts the name's length on the server, and length() counts CHARACTERS while octet_length(convert_to(...)) counts BYTES. For an ASCII name the two agree exactly, so an ASCII-only gate cannot tell a correct implementation from a broken one - and the disagreement it would miss is every guest read refusing. The scope's database name now carries two 2-byte characters, and the connection URI percent-encodes them.
